title: "Characterization of Bone Tumors in Computed Tomography and in Magnetic Resonance Imaging by Machine Learning"
summary:
Since primary bone tumors are a rather rare tumor entity, a correct and reliable assessment on conventional radiographs requires a great deal of experience. 
An incorrect categorization of a malignant bone tumor shortens the lifespan of a patient significantly. It is therefore important to optimize the diagnosis of bone tumors as best as possible. For clinicians or radiologists in particular, artificial intelligence could serve as decision support. The aim of the project is to use forms of machine learning to develop an artificial intelligence that can classify a bone tumor in terms of its dignity and, in a further step, can predict the tumor entity
conditions: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behaviour, unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients in tumor orthopedics at the LMU with a clinical diagnosis of a bone tumor (malignant/benign) and corresponding radiological examinations as well as histopathological findings/clinical diagnoses
Exclusion criteria:
